channel.title: Engineerspedia
channel.description: Engineering knowledge, without the jargon. Plain-language explainers spanning software, mechanical, civil, electrical, chemical and aerospace engineering.

item.title: How Wings Actually Generate Lift
item.description: Why the 'equal transit time' explanation of lift is wrong, and how circulation, angle of attack and Newton's third law actually keep an aircraft in the air.

item.title: Big-O Notation, Explained Without the Math Panic
item.description: A plain-language walkthrough of Big-O notation: what it measures, why it matters, and how to eyeball an algorithm's complexity.

item.title: Software Architecture Patterns, at a Glance
item.description: Monoliths, microservices, and everything between — a plain-language guide to picking a shape for your system.

item.title: Why Buildings Don't Fall Down: Load Paths 101
item.description: A plain-language tour of how structural loads travel from a roof to the ground, and what 'load-bearing' really means.

item.title: Circuit Design Basics: Volts, Amps, and Ohm's Law
item.description: The three numbers every circuit boils down to, and how to reason about voltage, current, and resistance with confidence.

item.title: Thermodynamics for People in a Hurry
item.description: The four laws of thermodynamics, explained with everyday examples instead of textbook notation.

item.title: How a Chemical Plant Actually Works
item.description: Following a raw material from tanker truck to finished product, one unit operation at a time.
